data: 1.1 Background
DocAI is designed to address the growing need for intelligent, secure, and context-aware
document retrieval systems. In today’s digital era, information is one of the most valuable
assets  for  organizations,

institutions,  and  businesses.  Whether 
it 
is  a  multinational
enterprise  or  a  small  educational  institution,  the  ability  to  store,  manage,  and  retrieve
knowledge effectively impacts decision-making, operational efficiency, and compliance.
It  is  important  to  remember  that  documentation—ranging  from  policy  guides,  training
manuals,  SOPs,  compliance  policies,  to  research  reports—represents  the  institutional
memory  of  an  organization.  Yet,  due  to  the  size  and  complexity  of  such  documents,
retrieval becomes a major challenge. Traditional methods like keyword search (Ctrl+F),
indexes,  and  bookmarks  are  still  common  but  operate  on  a  lexical  basis,  depending  on
exact word matches, which often leads to irrelevant or missed information.
To  understand
this  problem  more  deeply,  consider

that  corporate  HR 
teams, 
legal
professionals, or academic administrators regularly need to answer complex, multilayered
questions.  For  example,  an  HR  query  may  require  going  through  hundreds  of  pages  of
policy documents, while legal professionals might need to cross-reference internal SOPs,
legal  codes,  and  case  law.  In  these  cases,  keyword  search  often  fails  to  grasp  the  intent
behind  a  question.  The  emergence  of  Natural  Language  Processing  (NLP)  and  Large
Language  Models
(LLMs)  has

transformed 
this 
landscape  by  enabling  systems 
to
understand semantic meaning. This allows users to ask questions in natural language and
receive answers that are contextually appropriate, shifting from manual, inefficient methods
to  AI-powered  question-answering  systems  that  summarize,  explain,  or  extract  salient
points from large volumes of text.
To apply these advances, this project implements Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
to  accurately  respond  to  queries  from  internal  PDF  documents.  The  system  begins  by
preprocessing  documents  and  breaking  them  into  semantically  coherent  chunks.  These
chunks are then  embedded using a sentence transformer model,  allowing the system  to
numerically capture their meaning. The resulting vector embeddings are stored in a local
vector database, which enables rapid and efficient retrieval of relevant information. This
approach  ensures
that
the  system  remains  fully  offline,  aligning  with  privacy-first
principles and avoiding the use of external cloud services.
Analyzing  the  process  further,  when  a  user  submits  a  question,  the  system  performs  a
similarity search within the vector database to identify the most contextually relevant text
chunks. These are then passed to a locally hosted large language model, which uses them
as context to generate a grounded, precise answer. By using a local vector database and
on-premise inference, the system addresses concerns of data privacy, especially for sectors
